rationale:
The marked test `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/source_defaults.rs#fn[scoped_text_results_keep_line_numbers_context_and_completeness]` covers each obligation in `requirements.sdk.graph.search.TextQuery`.

- **Defaults:** `TextQuery::new(pattern)` is asserted to have `limit == None` and `context_lines == 0`. The default scope is checked by behaviour. The unscoped search finds all 3 matches across `one.txt` and `two.txt` and reports `complete`. Which files count as "visible" belongs to `source_scope`, not this requirement.
- **Zero context:** Every excerpt from the default query is exactly the 4-character matching line (`hit` plus a digit).
- **`pattern` as a regular expression:** The tests use `^hit[0-9]$` and `^hit$`, which depend on anchors and character classes.
- **`scope` override:** `.scope(SourceScope::under("one.txt"))` restricts the results to `one.txt` only. The entries are asserted exactly, including path and line.
- **`context_lines` override:** Context 1 is checked at the file start (`hit1\nmiddle`) and at the file end (`middle\nhit2`). Context 1 in the middle of `context.txt` gives `second\nhit\nfourth`. Context 2 gives `first` through `fifth`, which shows lines on both sides.
- **`limit` override:** `limit(2)` across the two-file scope gives 2 matches and `!complete`. `limit(1)` on the scoped query gives 1 match and `!complete`. A limit that is not exceeded (`limit(2)` on the scoped query, which has 2 hits) gives `complete`. `None` returns all matches.
- **Builders and fields:** Each builder method (`scope`, `context_lines`, `limit`) is used and its effect is observed. The `pattern`, `limit`, and `context_lines` fields are read directly.
- **Struct and method signatures:** The `#[non_exhaustive]` struct and the public signatures are covered by the marked `public_exports_match_the_appendix` export-inventory test, plus the consumer compile check.

I found no obligation without a test and no assertion that would accept behaviour the requirement forbids.

text: `TextQuery::new(pattern)` searches all visible files, with zero context lines and
no match limit. `scope`, `context_lines`, and `limit` override those defaults.

`pattern` is a regular expression. `context_lines` requests that many lines on either side of each matching line. Zero returns just the matching line. `limit` bounds matches across the scope. `None` requests all matches.
pub fn scope(self, scope: SourceScope) -> Self;
pub fn context_lines(self, context_lines: usize) -> Self;
pub fn limit(self, limit: usize) -> Self;
